\begin{abstract}
This supplement collects the Santander tables and figure, the MULAN selection rule, the implementation survey, the leaf-saturation checks, the synthetic study, the full MULAN dose-response table, and (Section~S7) the cap-sweep tables, tie attribution, all-product Instacart MLP, deployment protocol and train-row draws that the main text summarizes. Every number is a macro generated by \texttt{make\_tables.py} from the released result files; \texttt{REPRODUCE.md} maps each item to its result file and to the command that regenerates it.
\end{abstract}
\maketitle

\caption{\textbf{Elkan's shift holds exactly where the learner does not saturate and breaks where it does.} \textbf{A.} For each Santander label, the intended shift $\ln w_j$ against the label-free prevalence-matching shift $b_j$ of \Sm (the constant that returns the mean prediction to the training prevalence); the dashed line is $b_j=\ln w_j$, the behaviour Proposition~1 of the main text predicts. The \nSnIdentShift{} labels with no saturated cell lie on the line. On the other \nnCappedShift{} (triangles) $b_j$ is not identified at all: a cell at exactly $1.0$ cannot be moved by any finite shift, so it contributes a constant whatever $b$ is and the bisection settles near its bound. Those labels are drawn at the bound rather than at a value, because the value would be the clipping constant and not a property of the learner. \textbf{B.} Share of test cells at exactly $1.0$ per label against $\ln w_j$. \label{app:tau}
\Cref{tab:tau} reports the cross-validated selection for the default LightGBM at $w{=}1$; the result file covers all \nnTauCells{} learner--dataset cells. The rule ends more than $0.01$ below raw in \nnTauSelBelowRaw{} of them (\ntauFailCells): in each, the out-of-fold ranking of the candidates on the calibration split does not carry over to the standard test file of the benchmark, so the failure is one of the split, not of the rule.

\paragraph{Tie attribution.} The uncapped models tie instead of shifting, and how much that costs is dataset-dependent. On Santander \nStieCellsExactOne\% of cells sit at exactly $1.0$; \nStieRowsGeOne\% of rows contain at least one and \nStieRowsGeK\% at least $K$ (mean \nStieCellsPerRowMean{} per row). Re-ordering only those tied cells by the unweighted model's order returns \ntieShareUnw\% of the loss ($\nStieColumnOrder$ to $\nStieUnwOrder$) and an oracle order that reads the test labels \ntieShareOracle\% ($\nStieOracle$): on Santander the ties are the minor part and the ordered distortion is the rest, which is why per-label calibration recovers \nrepairShare\% of the loss. On Instacart the same measurement inverts. There \nIStieCellsExactOne\% of cells tie, \emph{every} row has at least $K$ of them (mean \nIStieCellsPerRowMean{} of \nInLabels{} labels), so the top-$K$ is decided entirely by how the sort breaks ties; re-ordering the tied cells by the unweighted order returns \nItieShareUnw\% of the loss ($\nIStieColumnOrder$ to $\nIStieUnwOrder$) and the oracle order reaches $\nIStieOracle$, above the unweighted model's own $\nItieNraw$. The collapse of the weighted Instacart model is therefore mostly a tie-breaking artefact of Lemma~1: no separable map can undo it, a per-label monotone map recovers what remains ordered, and a cap prevents it at training time.

\paragraph{Two estimators of the realized shift.} The label-free prevalence-matching shift $b_j$ is solved by bisection on $[-\nshiftSearchBound,\nshiftSearchBound]$ after clipping probabilities to $[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]$, so a clipped cell sits at $\pm\nshiftClipLogit$ nat and pins the solution near that bound whatever the learner did; every $b_j$ the main text quotes therefore comes from labels with no saturated cell. On those labels the booster's median $b_j/\ln w_j$ is $\nSbOverLnwMedian$ on Santander (\nSnIdentShift{} of \nnLabels{} labels, range $\nSbOverLnwMin$--$\nSbOverLnwMax$) and $\nISbOverLnwMedian$ on Instacart (\nISnIdentShift), and the Instacart MLP's is $\nIMSbOverLnwMedian$ (\nIMSnIdentShift{} of \nInLabels, range $\nIMSbOverLnwMin$--$\nIMSbOverLnwMax$); the Santander MLP retains a shift on \nMSnIdentShift{} label only, too few to quote a median. A second estimator with no bisection and no clipped cell --- the per-label median of $\operatorname{logit}\hat q-\operatorname{logit}\hat p$ over cells inside $(10^{-6},1-10^{-6})$ in both models --- admits any label with an unsaturated cell and so reads a larger set (\nSnDirectShift{} and \nISnDirectShift{} labels against \nSnIdentShift{} and \nISnIdentShift); it puts the two boosters at $\nSbDirectOverLnwMedian$ and $\nISbDirectOverLnwMedian$. The two instruments agree on the direction and neither reports a several-fold overshoot; they differ on how much of the shift is realized because they read different label sets. A cap only binds where $T\eta c<\ln w_j$; at the largest cap it does so for \nSmdsFivefracLnwAbove\% of Santander labels and \nISmdsFivefracLnwAbove\% of Instacart's. Capping the leaf step also costs capacity: at $c=0.7$ both the ceiling ($\nSmdsaceil$) and the within-label AUC ($\nSmdsaauc$) fall below the uncapped model's ($\nSceil$ and $\nSauc$), leaving the rare labels under-fitted (Table~S4).

\paragraph{The all-product Instacart MLP.} Scoring all \nIMAnLabels{} products in one shared-trunk MLP leaves \nIMASnDead{} of them without a positive in the calibration split (\nIMASnDeadVal{} in the validation period), with weights up to \nIMAwMax. There the identity fallback returns the weighted model exactly to its raw score ($\nIMASplIsoId$ against $\nIMASraw$) --- the takeover of Remark~2 at scale: the untouched labels are far more than $K$ per row and sit above the calibrated range --- while the prior fallback repairs it to $\nIMASplIsoPrior$ against a popularity baseline of $\nIMApopMAP$, and the deployment protocol gives $\ndepIMASplIsoPrior$. The unweighted arm of that pair learns nothing within a row (AUC $\nIMANauc$, raw $\nIMANraw$ at the popularity level, unchanged by any calibrator), while the weighted arm reaches $\nIMASauc$: at \nIMAnLabels{} labels the weight is what makes the model learn, and the fallback is what makes the ranking usable. This pair also meets the two conditions of Corollary~2 and the analytic inversion pays there too ($\nIMASraw$ to $\nIMASelkan$).

\paragraph{Deployment protocol on Instacart.} The deployment protocol calibrates on each user's second-last order and evaluates on the last. It moves the weighted model from $\ndepISraw$ to $\ndepISplIsoPrior$ and the unweighted one from $\ndepINraw$ to $\ndepINplIsoPrior$, within $\ndepISCeilGap$ and $\ndepINCeilGap$ of their ceilings ($\ndepISceil$ and $\ndepINceil$), with \ndepISnDeadVal{} labels lacking positives in the validation orders; both differ from the test-split rungs of Table~1 of the main text by at most $\nIprotoMaxDiffPair$ and keep their order. On Santander (Table~S3) \Sm goes from $\ndepSraw$ to $\ndepSplIsoPrior$ (\ndepSrepairShare\% of its loss against \Nm, whose raw score is $\ndepNraw$), the intercept-only shift returns \ndepSoffsetShare\%, \Nm changes by $\ndepNprGain$, and \ndepSnDeadVal{} labels have no positives in the validation period; on the per-label isotonic rung the two protocols differ by at most $\nprotoMaxDiff$.

\paragraph{Train-row draws.} Retraining both LightGBM pairs on \nseedN{} independent 90\% draws of the training rows separates what is stable from what is not (mean $\pm$ SD over the draws). The quantity that moves is the weighted model's raw score: $\nseedSraw$ on Santander, a spread of the same order as the score itself, because how far each label saturates depends on which rows the draw keeps ($\nseedSsatOne\%$ of cells at exactly $1.0$). The two rungs closest to it move with it, the analytic inversion and pooled isotonic, both of which read the depth of the saturation. Everything else the paper reads off the ladder is stable: the unweighted raw score is $\nseedNraw$, the repaired weighted model $\nseedSplIsoPrior$ against a ceiling of $\nseedSceil$, the unweighted model under the same calibrator $\nseedNplIsoPrior$, and the odds share $\nseedOddsShare\%$ against the \noddsShare\% of the matched pair. Instacart is stable throughout, including its raw scores ($\nIseedSraw$ and $\nIseedNraw$, repaired $\nIseedSplIsoPrior$ and $\nIseedNplIsoPrior$, odds share $\nIseedOddsShare\%$, saturation $\nIseedSsatOne\%$). The decomposition and the ladder are therefore properties of the configuration, not of one draw; only the depth of the weighted model's collapse depends on the sample. An earlier run of the weighted Santander configuration (Table~S4) differs from \Sm by $\nSorigMinusS$ in raw $\mapseven$ and behaves the same on every rung.


\section{Proofs}
\label{app:proofs}
\paragraph{Shared and distinct separable maps (Remark~1).} Let $g_1,\dots,g_L$ be non-decreasing maps on a common interval $I$. (a) If $g_1=\dots=g_L$, the separable calibrator never creates a strict inversion: $s_{ij}>s_{ik}$ implies $\tilde s_{ij}\ge\tilde s_{ik}$, with equality only when both scores fall in the same plateau of the shared map; this is monotonicity. (b) If the maps are continuous and $g_j(a)<g_k(a)$ for some interior $a\in I$, continuity of $g_j$ gives $b>a$ in $I$ with $g_j(b)<g_k(a)$, and the row with $s_{ij}=b>a=s_{ik}$ has $\tilde s_{ij}<\tilde s_{ik}$. If no such $b$ exists because $a$ is the right endpoint, use continuity of $g_k$ to pick $b<a$ with $g_k(b)>g_j(a)$ and the row $s_{ik}=b<a=s_{ij}$.

\paragraph{Proposition~1 (odds shift).} The weighted loss is the unweighted loss under the tilted distribution whose posterior odds are $w_j$ times the original; the flip condition is the difference of the shifted logits.

\paragraph{Lemma~1 (leaf saturation).} $-wn_+\ln\rho-n_-\ln(1-\rho)$ is minimized at $\rho=wn_+/(wn_++n_-)$, and $1-\rho=n_-/(wn_++n_-)\le n_-/(wn_+)$.

\paragraph{Proposition~2 (step budget).} Each round adds at most $\eta c$ in absolute value, so the first two bounds telescope. The mean of $\sigma(F^{w}_j(x_i)-b)$ over $i$ is decreasing in $b$; at $b=T\eta c$ every argument is at most $\operatorname{logit}\hat\pi_j$, so the mean is at most $\hat\pi_j$, and at $b=-T\eta c$ it is at least $\hat\pi_j$; the solution therefore lies in $[-T\eta c,T\eta c]$. The last claim compares the realized shift with the shift of Proposition~1.

\paragraph{Corollary~2 (when the inversion is exact).} The inverted score of label $j$ at $x$ is $F^{0}_j(x)+\delta_j(x)$. If $\delta_j(x)$ does not depend on $j$ it shifts every label of the row equally and leaves the within-row order of $F^{0}$ unchanged; $\delta\equiv0$ is the special case. Under a cap, write $D_j(x)=F^{w}_j(x)-F^{0}_j(x)$, so $|D_j|\le 2T\eta c$ by Proposition~2: pointwise equality is $D_j(x)=\ln w_j$, giving $\ln w_j\le 2T\eta c$; a row-constant residual gives $\ln w_j-\ln w_k=D_j(x)-D_k(x)$, which bounds the spread $\max_j\ln w_j-\min_j\ln w_j$ by $4T\eta c$ and leaves the magnitude free, which is why a common weight (Corollary~1(a)) escapes the bound entirely.
